_meta._image_lane_added_2026_08_10: The `image` lane, and with it the office's FIRST image-capable providers. Read the lane's own `_the_designer_had_never_worked` and `_why_roles_and_not_primary_backup` notes before changing anything in it. Two structural rules changed with it, both in `workers/task-router.js`: (1) A ROUTABLE LANE MUST NOW DECLARE `kind`. It used to be optional, and the wrong-kind check was written `if (lane.kind && ...)` — so a lane that simply omitted the field accepted ANY provider. That was harmless while every provider was chat or embeddings and became a real hazard the moment an image provider entered the registry, because a kind-less text lane would have resolved to an image model and returned an envelope with no `text` in it. A lane with no kind is now refused as `lane_kind_unstated`. (2) `assignEmbodiment()` now RECORDS every pool member it drops for wrong kind, in `poolExcluded`, instead of filtering it out silently — a shuffle that quietly discards half its pool still returns a well-formed map, which is this project's most-repeated defect shape. `scripts/verify-routing.js` §8 proves both against a transcription of the pre-change logic.
_meta.status: ENABLED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-10, after the supervised test's Steps 3a-3i were run end to end. It shipped OFF on 2026-08-05 and stayed inert for five days. THIS FIELD IS A CLAIM ABOUT PRODUCTION AND GOES STALE THE MOMENT SOMEONE TOGGLES THE FLAG — read the live state back with `{"type":"routing_status"}` rather than trusting this string. That rule is boarded as OB-040 and this line is an instance of exactly what it is about.
_meta._enabled_2026_08_10: The supervised test found TWO defects that an HTTP 200 hid, both fixed before the switch was flipped. (1) An empty answer was returned as a SUCCESS: routeTask() tested only `if (result)`, so a 200 carrying an empty string came back ok:true with no degradation — and `finishReason` had been added to the envelope specifically to prevent that and was never read by anything. (2) Cerebras' gpt-oss-120b is a REASONING model whose thinking is charged against max_tokens, so the judgment lane — 'short scored calls', the shape a caller naturally gives a small budget — returned empty at max_tokens 64 and '0.8' at 600. See workers/task-router.js routeTask() and workers/cerebras-client.js MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS.
_meta.description: The task-type routing table. Lanes are DATA, deliberately, so changing which provider serves a task is a config edit rather than a code edit — workers/task-router.js reads this file and contains no per-lane conditionals of its own. Routing by TASK TYPE, never by agent: a persona's voice lives in its prompts and character files (back-office-AI-agents/campus/agents/<NN-slug>/), never in which key answered.
_meta.the_overtime_rule: Every provider here is on its FREE TIER and stays there. A call that would exceed a free tier is REFUSED and logged as `overtime_required`. There is no automatic escalation to a paid tier, for any provider, ever — paid usage requires the owner's explicit, per-instance approval, asked for at the time.
_meta.anthropic_is_not_here: Anthropic has no lane, no pool entry, and no registry entry. The `architect` lane below exists to STATE that rule where someone would look to break it, not to enable it — it carries `routable: false` and no provider id. Two independent barriers enforce this: (1) resolveLane() refuses a non-routable lane, and (2) workers/task-router.js's PROVIDER_REGISTRY imports no Anthropic client, so a lane naming one fails closed as `unknown_provider`. scripts/verify-routing.js proves both, including by pointing a lane at 'anthropic' on purpose and asserting it is denied.

github-models.reason: GitHub Models was FULLY RETIRED on 2026-07-30 — playground, catalog, inference API and BYOK, permanently, for all customers. Not a brownout, not a degraded tier, not a bad key: the catalog and inference endpoints both return HTTP 410 WITHOUT an Authorization header, which is what proves the service is gone rather than the credential rejected.
github-models.found_by: The supervised test procedure's Step 1 (back-office-AI-agents/docs/procedures/ROUTING-SUPERVISED-TEST.md), run 2026-08-06 — the FIRST time any model ID in this table was checked against a live catalog.
github-models.do_not_re_add: The 410 response body still reads 'temporarily unavailable ... scheduled retirement brownout'. That text is STALE — it outlived the service it describes. Trust the retirement date, not the error string. Anything re-adding this provider on the strength of the word 'temporarily' is reading a tombstone as a status page.
github-models.what_was_removed: the lane primary (judgment), the conversation pool entry, the PROVIDER_REGISTRY entry in workers/task-router.js, the providers.github_models block in config/token-economy.json, and workers/github-models-client.js (deleted). The GITHUB_MODELS_TOKEN Cloudflare secret is the owner's to delete — no session holds secret-write authority.

_meta.supersedes: plans/OFFICE-SCALING-TODO.md item 3.1's four-lane draft table and PROJECT-SPEC-TABLES.md's matching row, both of which predate this session: neither had a long-document lane or an embeddings lane, and both backed Hebrew composition with GitHub Models rather than Mistral. Both documents are corrected in the same session as this file, per the spec-tables maintenance rule.

switch._meta: Mirrors the `guides_enabled` pattern (workers/agent-runner.js guidesEnabled(), added 2026-08-02), which is the proven shape in this repo for shipping a feature dark. Absent or false means the router refuses every routed call with `routing_disabled` and every pre-existing caller keeps its current provider untouched. Toggle without a redeploy: POST /api/agents/trigger {"type":"routing_toggle","enabled":true|false}.

_soft_stop_fraction_meta: A provider is refused once its counted calls for the day reach this fraction of its KNOWN free-tier daily cap — not at 100%. Two reasons. (1) It directly serves Gate 3 in plans/OFFICE-SCALING-TODO.md, whose acceptance criterion is '48h of live routing logs reviewed; no provider over 60% of its free-tier daily quota' — the router should KEEP the office under that line rather than let the owner discover a breach afterwards. (2) It mirrors the deliberate-headroom convention the Anthropic budget already uses ($4.50 soft-stop under a $5 ceiling). Raising it is a config edit and an owner decision.
_unknown_cap_meta: A NULL daily cap in config/token-economy.json's `providers` block means THIS REPO DOES NOT KNOW the limit. It does NOT mean unlimited, and the router must never treat it as such (owner instruction, 2026-08-05). Since an unknown cap cannot be enforced by counting, it is enforced by WALL CLOCK instead: a provider with no known daily cap gets a minimum spacing between routed calls, tracked by a KV timestamp. The mechanism and the 20s floor are lifted from workers/gemini-pacer.js, which solves the same problem for the same reason — a quota this repo cannot observe. Once a real cap is established by the supervised test, fill it into token-economy.json and the count check takes over automatically; nothing here needs editing.

judgment.description: Judgment / quality — QA (agent 6), Lead QA (agent 8) and Team Lead (agent 7) reviews. Short scored calls.
judgment._why: REPOINTED 2026-08-06. This lane originally ran GitHub Models primary with Cerebras behind it, chosen because GitHub Models' ~8K-token per-request ceiling was a poor fit for bulk text but a fine fit for 'score this answer 0-1'. GitHub Models was permanently RETIRED on 2026-07-30 (see _provider_removals below), so the backup was promoted and Mistral moved in behind it. Cerebras' 131K context means this lane no longer has a per-request ceiling that a long judgment call can overflow — the reason the old table needed the long-context lane as its backup no longer applies.
judgment._concentration_risk: This lane and `long_document` now share a PRIMARY (cerebras) AND a BACKUP (mistral). One Cerebras outage takes out both lanes at once, and both then land on the same Mistral free tier — the failure concentrates rather than spreads. Owner-accepted on 2026-08-06 rather than papered over. The intended diversification IF IT BITES is OpenRouter as a third chat provider, so the two lanes can hold different primaries again; it is deliberately NOT added now, because adding a provider to solve a risk that has not materialised spends a free tier and a secret on a hypothetical.

long_document.description: Long-document processing — daily report batches, cross-report input, anything past what a single judgment call should carry.
long_document._context_ceiling: Cerebras' real per-request input limit was MEASURED on 2026-08-06 at 131000 tokens (gpt-oss-120b) and is now enforced client-side. It was null — unknown — until then, on the lane whose entire job is long input. See workers/cerebras-client.js for the read-back.
long_document._concentration_risk: See `judgment._concentration_risk` — the two lanes share both providers.

hebrew_composition.description: Hebrew composition — capability-gap notes and internal summaries, in the flagging agent's own voice.
hebrew_composition._why: Hebrew here is INTERNAL only. The Front is English only (owner decision, 2026-08-05), so this lane never touches published content. Gemini stays primary; workers/gemini-pacer.js's 20s spacing on Notebook-X asks remains in force and routing does not get to spend the headroom that pacing deliberately leaves.

front_localization.description: Front localization — re-voicing internal Hebrew office material (capability-gap notes, meeting minutes, report summaries) into English narrative for the public Front. Closes the `front-localization` capability CAPABILITY-TOOLBOX.md listed UNSUPPLIED against Agent 9 since 2026-08-10.
front_localization._new_lane_not_an_extension_and_why: A NEW lane, deliberately, not a parameter added to `hebrew_composition`. `hebrew_composition` WRITES Hebrew; this is the only thing in this repo that carries content the other direction, and the two must never be reachable from the same call site under the same name — a caller asking for `front_localization` by name cannot be silently handed a Hebrew-writing prompt by a future edit that merges the two. Same reasoning `report_drafting` used when it was split out from `routine_volume` rather than reusing it with a flag.
front_localization._why_gemini_primary: Same providers as `hebrew_composition` (gemini primary, mistral backup) — Gemini is already the office's proven multilingual, in-persona composer, not merely the default pick. Sharing the pool means front_localization draws against the SAME already-paced Gemini key as `hebrew_composition`, `report_drafting`, the image `polish` role and the Notebook-X asks (see `image._shared_allowances_stated_up_front`) — a fifth consumer on a key `workers/gemini-pacer.js` already paces at 20s. Stated here so a future session does not add a sixth without reading this.
front_localization._no_production_caller_yet: Same shape as the `embeddings` lane before it had a caller: built, verified, resolvable, and reachable only through `workers/localization-engine.js` `localizeForFront()` and the supervised `{"type":"localization_test"}` trigger today. The Front page that will call it in production is OB-013's to build, not this session's.

report_drafting.description: Report drafting — the office's weekly and monthly reports, written by The Workflow (agent 12) and reviewed by the QA on the judgment lane.
report_drafting._why: OWNER DECISION AD-028 (2026-08-08), IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-09. Reports are drafted by Gemini, and this lane is how that holds once routing is switched on. It exists because the alternative was pinning the provider at the call site, and a lane keeps the rule as DATA, where a future session would actually edit it. Before this lane existed, report drafting resolved to `routine_volume`, whose primary is Groq — so an English report would have been drafted by Groq the moment routing was enabled, silently breaking the requirement while every test still passed.
report_drafting._do_not: Do NOT delete this lane and point report drafting back at `routine_volume` as a simplification, and do NOT repoint `routine_volume`'s primary to gemini to make the two agree. That lane's primary is Groq by design and serves every other routine caller; report drafting is exempt by owner decision, and the exemption is the point rather than an oversight. workers/report-pipeline.js planReportProviders() reads this lane's resolved primary at runtime and reports geminiRequirementHolds=false if it is anything but gemini.
report_drafting._language: Language-independent, deliberately. Hebrew report drafting resolves here too, not to `hebrew_composition`: making the pin conditional on language reintroduces a path where the requirement quietly stops holding, and both lanes name gemini primary in any case.

routine_volume.description: Routine volume — drafts, coworker chatter, spare-time interactions.
routine_volume._why: This lane is already exactly what agents/agent-base.js queryGroqRouted() does today (Groq first, Cloudflare Workers AI on failure). It is written down here so the table is complete, not to change anything.

classification.description: Classification / routing decisions — short triage tags, category labels.

conversation.description: Conversations & office events — meetings, standups, side plots. The persona→provider assignment is shuffled per event and the resulting embodiment map is logged.
conversation._why_random: This is a MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT, not a fallback mechanism. The Lead QA (agent 8) compares report quality across agents AND across embodiment models — 'this persona is more consistent under that provider', 'that provider invents facts in meetings'. Shuffling is what generates the comparison data; logging the map is what makes it readable. If this ever gets quietly replaced by a fixed assignment, the cross-embodiment half of the improvement loop stops producing evidence and nothing else will notice.
conversation._pool_excludes_cohere: cohere is an embeddings provider and cannot serve a chat lane. The registry's `kind` check enforces this independently of this list; verify-routing.js asserts the pool contains no embeddings provider.

image.description: Visual assets — the Designer (agent 9). TWO ROLES, not a primary and a backup: `draft` is Cloudflare Workers AI, `polish` is Gemini. Owner decision, 2026-08-10.
image._why_roles_and_not_primary_backup: OWNER DECISION, 2026-08-10: 'Cloudflare Workers AI by default, Gemini for polish and final touches.' Those are two different JOBS, and `primary`/`backup` cannot express that — that pair means 'the same job, second choice'. Written as primary+backup, a Cloudflare outage would silently send every DRAFT to the polish provider and spend the scarcer free tier on throwaway work, while a caller asking for POLISH would get a fresh draft back and never learn that the image it asked to improve was never looked at. So the lane carries a `roles` map and resolveLane() takes a `role` option; each role resolves to exactly ONE candidate.
image._why_a_role_never_degrades_to_the_other_: A CORRECTNESS rule, the same family as `embeddings._why_no_backup`, and it fails the same way — confidently. A polish pass answered by a fresh draft returns a plausible image that is not the thing that was asked for. `workers/gemini-image-client.js` polishImage() REFUSES a call with no input image for this reason, so the rule is enforced in the client as well as in the routing table. Two independent barriers; deleting one does not open the path.
image._the_designer_had_never_worked: This lane is why. `AGENTS-CHARACTER-CORE-v2.md` AGENT 9 has said since 2026-08-05 that she 'generates visual assets through the office's image-capable providers, always leaving a provenance note (model, date)'. NO IMAGE-CAPABLE PROVIDER WAS WIRED ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO until 2026-08-10 — plan 5.1 specified one and it was never built, and OB-013, OB-014, OB-015 and REQ-002 all sat behind it. That is a NEW VARIANT of this project's dominant defect (ARCHITECTURAL-DECISIONS.md §7): not a gate that is never called, but A ROLE THAT WAS NEVER ACTIVATED. Documentation asserted a capability; no code path supplied it.
image._why_nobody_caught_it: `workers/meeting-decisions.js` computeWorkflowMetrics() measures who has not worked from ACTIVITY rows and from DISPATCHED tasks. The Designer was never dispatched anything and her Q&A asks kept her activity row warm, so she never read as idle — SHE READ AS ABSENT FROM THE QUESTION. A census can only see a role that stopped working. The second mechanism, which sees a role that never started, is `workers/capability-audit.js`: for every agent, does a code path supply the means its role requires?
image._free_tier_only: Both providers are free-tier and stay there. Cloudflare's allowance is denominated in NEURONS, not requests, and the binding does not report a balance — so `requests_per_day` is null and the router paces this provider by wall clock instead of counting. Gemini's image request ceiling is not in a readable header, so it is null for the same reason. A null cap means THIS REPO DOES NOT KNOW, never 'unlimited'. `overtime_required` is a refusal and there is no escalation to a paid tier, for any provider, ever.
image._shared_allowances_stated_up_front: NEITHER provider here has an allowance of its own. `cloudflare-images` spends the SAME account Workers AI Neurons as `cloudflare-ai`, which is the classification lane's PRIMARY and routine_volume's BACKUP. `gemini-images` spends the SAME API key as `hebrew_composition`, `report_drafting`, the report synthesis and the Notebook-X asks — a key `workers/gemini-pacer.js` already paces at 20s because two consumers this repo cannot observe share it; image calls are a third. Heavy Designer output can therefore degrade FOUR chat lanes. Recorded here rather than discovered during an incident, the same way the cerebras two-lane concentration risk is.

embeddings.description: Embeddings / semantic search — the local brain's search and cross-report comparison. Neither is built yet, so this lane has no callers.
embeddings._why_no_backup: Fail, do not degrade — a CORRECTNESS rule, not a preference. Vectors from two different embedding models do not share a space, so a similarity computed across them is meaningless while still returning a confident-looking number between 0 and 1. Substituting a backup would corrupt a search index rather than slow it down.

architect.description: The Architect (agent 10). NEVER routed, NEVER shuffled.
architect._why: He runs on the Anthropic API exclusively, per the character bible, and Anthropic is reserved for him and for genuine data-center Q&A under its own capped budget. This lane is present so that the rule is visible in the table a future session would edit to break it — it names no provider, and resolveLane() refuses it. His actual call paths (workers/claude-client.js and the APP_API service binding) are direct callers that never went through this router and are untouched by it.
